name: Midwestern Cream Slaw (Coleslaw)

cookwares.name: salad spinner or baking sheet lined with paper towels or clean kitchen towels

instructions.primary_message: In a large bowl, toss cabbage and carrot with the salt until well combined. Let sit for 15 minutes, then transfer to a colander and rinse thoroughly under cold running water. Spin the slaw dry in a salad spinner, or transfer it to a baking sheet lined with paper towels or clean kitchen towels and blot dry with more paper towels or a clean kitchen towel.

Rinse and dry the bowl, then add heavy cream and sugar and whisk until sugar is dissolved. Slowly whisk in vinegar; the dressing will thicken slightly. Whisk in mustard, white pepper, and celery seed.
Add cabbage and carrots to the dressing and toss to coat. Season with salt to taste, if needed. Cover, transfer to the refrigerator, and let sit at least 2 hours and up to 24 hours before serving.

schema_metadata.keywords: Midwestern Cream Slaw, coleslaw recipe, Midwestern Coleslaw

description: Coleslaw gets a vintage twist in this mayo-free cream slaw, with a simple cream-and-vinegar dressing that's tangy and light on the perfectly crisp cabbage. It's right at home at cookouts, potlucks, picnics, and more.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 2 hr 20 min.

Notes: This recipe is easiest to produce with a mandoline-style slicer, though you can also finely shred the cabbage by hand. To slice cabbages on a mandoline, split the head in half, cut out the core with the tip of a sharp chef's knife, then quarter the cabbage and slice it with the mandoline set to 1/16-inch thickness.

Make-ahead and storage: The coleslaw can be refrigerated for up to 1 day before serving.
author: Jed Portman
